# Read operations

The <kbd>SmemNode</kbd> interface provides two primary methods for reading data: <kbd>search()</kbd> for semantic (vector) search and <kbd>filter()</kbd> for filtering by non-vector columns.

## Semantic Search

To perform a semantic search, use the <kbd>search()</kbd> method on a node. It accepts a query string and optional search parameters:

```ts
const results = await mem.nodes.documents.search("lorem ipsum", {
    limit: 10,
    select: ["title", "text"],
    distanceType: "cosine",
});
```

The <kbd>results</kbd> array contains matching records with a <kbd>_distance</kbd> field indicating similarity. Lower distances indicate higher similarity.

### Search Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `limit` | `number` | Maximum number of results (default: `-1` for all) |
| `select` | `string[]` | Columns to include in results (empty = all columns) |
| `distanceType` | `string` | Distance metric: `"cosine"` or `"l2"` |
| `filters` | `string[]` | Filter expressions applied before search |

## Vector Embeddings

To get the raw embedding vector for a text string, use the <kbd>vector()</kbd> method:

```ts
const embedding = await mem.vector("hello world");
// Returns: Array<number> (384-dimensional)
```

This is useful when you need to pass pre-computed vectors to other systems or perform custom similarity calculations.

## Filters

To filter by non-vector columns without semantic search, use the <kbd>filter()</kbd> method:

```ts
const results = await mem.nodes.documents.filter({
    limit: 20,
    select: ["title", "text"],
    filters: ["tags LIKE '%science%'"],
});
```

The <kbd>filters</kbd> parameter accepts an array of SQL-like filter expressions. These are applied to non-vector columns only.

### Filter Examples

```ts
// String match
const results = await mem.nodes.documents.filter({
    filters: ["title = 'Hello World'"],
});

// Numeric comparison
const results = await mem.nodes.documents.filter({
    filters: ["id > 5", "score >= 0.8"],
});

// Combined filters
const results = await mem.nodes.documents.filter({
    filters: ["category = 'physics'", "year > 2020"],
});
```

## Search with Filters

You can combine semantic search with column filters by including the <kbd>filters</kbd> parameter in the search call:

```ts
const results = await mem.nodes.documents.search("quantum computing", {
    limit: 5,
    select: ["title", "text"],
    distanceType: "cosine",
    filters: ["category = 'science'"],
});
```

## Raw Table Access

For advanced operations not covered by the <kbd>search()</kbd> and <kbd>filter()</kbd> methods, you can access the underlying LanceDB <kbd>Table</kbd> object directly:

```ts
const table = await mem.openTable("documents");
// Use the LanceDB Table API directly
// See https://lancedb.github.io/lancedb/guides/tables/ for more info
```
